name: pivot_support_resistance
author: Kakushadze and Serur, 151 Trading Strategies, section 3.14
timeframe: 1-hour bars, levels from the previous UTC day
entry_rule: Pivot C = (previous day's high + low + close) / 3. Go long when a bar closes above C after the previous bar closed at or below it. Go short when a bar closes below C after the previous bar closed at or above it.
exit_rule: Book: exit a long at R = 2C - previous low, exit a short at S = 2C - previous high. The lab uses its own fixed exits instead.
reason: Not stated in the book. Common explanation: many traders watch the same daily levels, so price reacts around them.
who_loses: Traders who fade a move through a widely watched level.

name: channel_bounce
author: Kakushadze and Serur, 151 Trading Strategies, section 3.15
entry_rule: Ceiling and floor are the highest and lowest close of the previous T bars. Go long when a bar closes at or below the floor. Go short when a bar closes at or above the ceiling.
exit_rule: Book: reverse at the opposite band. The lab uses its own fixed exits instead.
reason: Price inside a range tends to bounce off its edges.
who_loses: Breakout traders who enter at the edge of a range that holds.

name: ibs_reversion
author: Kakushadze and Serur, 151 Trading Strategies, section 4.4
timeframe: 1-hour bars, signal from the previous UTC day
entry_rule: IBS = (previous day's close - low) / (high - low). On the first bar of a new day, go long if IBS is below the threshold and go short if IBS is above 1 minus the threshold. The book sorts many ETFs by IBS and trades the extremes against each other; this is a single-market adaptation.
exit_rule: Not stated beyond daily rebalancing. The lab uses its own fixed exits.
reason: A close near the day's low is 'cheap' and a close near the high is 'rich', and short-term extremes tend to revert.
who_loses: Traders who need to sell or buy urgently into the close and pay for immediacy.
